title: Lay out and test a CMOS inverter
concept: The PMOS and NMOS occupy separate rows. Their drains meet on Y, and their bodies reach the two power rails through the terminal contacts.
question: Which physical connection joins the two drains?
explanation: Y connects both drain contacts through Metal 2 drops and vias to its shared Metal 3 track.
focus: Trace the A drops to the two gates and Y to the two drains. Each body contact should reach its own rail.
reflection: Explain how the Y route joins the drain contacts. Compare the schematic and layout-loaded waveforms and report the extra estimated load on Y.

title: Lay out and test a two-input NAND
concept: The NMOS stack has an internal diffusion connection called N_STACK. Separate contacts let you see which nets reach the cell pins and which stay inside it.
question: Which connection stays internal to the NAND cell?
explanation: N_STACK joins the two NMOS devices. The output is low only at A=1 and B=1.
focus: Trace the NMOS series path from Y to N_STACK to VGND. N_STACK has a Metal 3 track without a left-edge port.
reflection: Show where N_STACK stays internal and which input vector pulls Y down. Describe how series devices and added metal capacitance affect the falling edge.

title: Lay out and test a two-input NOR
concept: The PMOS pull-up uses a series connection. Its internal P_STACK track must remain separate from the upper supply rail.
question: Where does P_STACK connect in the layout?
explanation: P_STACK joins the PMOS stack. Both PMOS gates must be low for the stack to charge Y.
focus: Follow VPWR into the upper row, then trace P_STACK between the PMOS devices and Y at the far side of the stack.
reflection: Compare the NOR pull-up layout with the NAND pull-down layout. Identify the vector that charges Y and note the layout-added load.

title: Lay out and test an AND-OR-invert cell
concept: AOI21 merges two distinct pull-down paths at Y. C drives a direct branch and the A/B path uses a series stack.
question: Which routed input alone should force Y low?
explanation: A high on C enables a direct pull-down branch to VGND and blocks the complementary pull-up.
focus: Follow the C track to both device rows. Identify P_BRANCH and N_STACK under the output routes.
reflection: Trace the branch that lets C override A and B. Use one captured vector and the routed output load to explain the observed transition.

title: Lay out and test a transmission-gate multiplexer
concept: The transmission gates need separate S and S_B conductors. Metal 2 drops cross Metal 3 tracks, with a via only where they connect.
question: What connects a Metal 2 drop to a crossing Metal 3 track?
options: A via between the two layers
explanation: A via makes the layer transition. The separated S and S_B nets control which data input reaches the buffered output.
focus: Locate the S and S_B tracks and the internal SELECTED node. Check where the output buffer drives Y.
reflection: Compare S and S_B routes and show how each data input reaches Y. Compare a switching edge in the two saved models.

title: Lay out and test a rising-edge D flip-flop
concept: The master and slave latches use CLK and CLK_B on distinct conductors. Q also feeds back into the slave latch, so the output route connects an internal path and the external pin.
question: Which pair of clock tracks needs separate routing?
explanation: The complementary CLK and CLK_B tracks enable different paths on each phase. Q captures on the rising edge and holds between edges.
focus: Follow CLK and CLK_B through the large cell. Locate the Q track where the slave output and feedback meet.
reflection: Use the layout and the captured samples to explain how Q feeds the slave loop, captures on rising edges, and holds when D changes.

title: Fit an inverter into a 12.8 µm cell
concept: Neighboring cells share the same rail heights. Reduce the horizontal device pitch so this inverter fits its width budget and still switches correctly.
question: Which edit reduces the cell width while leaving the shared rail heights fixed?
explanation: A smaller device pitch brings the two device columns closer together. The boundary and routing still have to pass the physical checks.
focus: Measure the 13.8 µm starter outline. Change the horizontal pitch and compare the revised boundary.
tune: Reduce Horizontal device pitch, rebuild the layout, and finish the missing routes again.
solution: Set Horizontal device pitch to 4.8 µm. The footprint is 12.8 µm wide. Both input levels must still pass with the 10 fF fixture.
reflection: Record the starter and final widths. Explain how you reduced the width while keeping the same power-rail heights and passing the logic test.

title: Drive 40 fF with a faster NAND
concept: A NAND discharges through two series NMOS devices. With A held high, the rising B edge isolates the delay through this path into a 40 fF load.
question: Which change directly reduces resistance in the loaded NAND pull-down?
explanation: Wider devices reduce channel resistance. The loaded B-to-Y edge measures whether the pull-down is fast enough.
focus: Locate MN_A and MN_B on the N_STACK path from Y to VGND.
tune: Increase the NMOS stack width, rebuild, and rerun the 40 fF test.
solution: Set NMOS stack width to 2 µm. At the applied 40 fF load, check that B rising to Y falling takes at most 100 ps and all four logic vectors pass.
reflection: Record the delay before and after sizing the series pair. Explain why the test holds A high while B switches.

title: Meet the flip-flop clock-to-Q budget
concept: The Q inverter must drive 40 fF within a clock-to-output delay budget. The combined output-driver width limits how much you can enlarge the two devices.
question: Which input transition starts the clock-to-Q delay measurement?
options: The rising clock crossing at half the supply
A falling D edge while the clock is high
explanation: Start at the rising clock crossing and stop at the corresponding Q crossing. Measure rising and falling Q separately.
focus: Find the Q driver, MN_Q and MP_Q, at the end of the slave latch.
tune: Adjust the two Q driver widths separately. Check both clock-to-Q delay readings and their combined width before rerunning.
solution: Set the Q NMOS width to 2 µm and the Q PMOS width to 3.5 µm. The combined width is 5.5 µm. Verify Q rise at or below 185 ps and Q fall at or below 128 ps, with capture and hold intact.
reflection: Record both clock-to-Q measurements and your combined driver width. Explain how you divided the width budget between the NMOS and PMOS.
